_comment: Per-fund KpkSharesRouter deployments. One router per KpkShares proxy.
The limits below are STARTING VALUES, not decided risk policy. Whoever owns fund risk must review
them before the router is wired, because once atomic settlement is live they are the only economic
protection continuing shareholders have (see the contract-level NatSpec in KpkSharesRouter.sol).
priceFloor / priceCeil are absolute 8-decimal bounds that do NOT track the fund's last settled
price, which is what makes them resistant to the per-call deviation ratchet. A growing fund will
eventually push priceCeil, and raising it is a deliberate admin action — that is the intent.
maxNavTtl is the primary lever on stale-NAV arbitrage and doubles as the kill switch: if the
pricing service stops signing, atomic settlement stops on its own. It bounds a quote in BOTH
directions — validUntil may not exceed now + maxNavTtl, and the price may not be older than
DAILY CAPS ARE FIXED UTC WINDOWS, so the true bound on any rolling 24h is 2x the value set here
(a full budget at 23:59 and another at 00:00), and they are PER ASSET, so two enabled assets
double it again. The values below are halved relative to the intended rolling-day bound: 2.5M
configured => 5M per rolling day per asset => 10M across USDC+USDT. Re-derive if the asset set
maxFeeDilutionBps bounds PERFORMANCE-fee dilution only. kUSD runs performanceFeeModule = 0x0, so
on this fund the guard never fires; management-fee dilution (300 bps/yr) is bounded operationally
by settlement cadence, not on-chain. Keep settlements frequent.

routers._adminNote: Must be whichever Safe holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the fund at wiring time. As of docs/DEPLOYED_ADDRESSES.md that is the staging Sec Council Safe, with a handover to the production Sec Council pending — sequence the OPERATOR grant against whichever holds the role then.
routers._guardianNote: Manager Safe. Add an ops hot key as a second GUARDIAN_ROLE holder so pausing does not need a multisig round trip.
